correction: The NvPCR masks were justified only by systemd 261's anchor secret, which cannot migrate between PCR signing keys and becomes unreadable after a TPM replacement. systemd 262 removed the anchor secret entirely: tpm2-setup now deletes the old anchor credentials. NvPCRs are now created in the initrd under a write policy that needs every definition inside the UKI and a ukify --sign-initrd-pcrs initrd policy. The masks still apply, because the unit and definition names are unchanged and tpm2-setup still filters masked definitions. They are also still needed, because snosi UKIs carry neither requirement. The old rationale no longer describes the mechanism.
evidence: systemd v262 NEWS 'Changes in the TPM Subsystem'; v262 src/tpm2-setup/tpm2-setup.c setup_nvpcr (initrd-only, CONF_FILES_FILTER_MASKED) and cleanup_old_nvpcr_creds; systemd-tpm 261.2-1 vs 262-1 deb diff (units identical, hardware.nvpcr gains orderly:false); floe 262 initramfs has no nvpcr definitions; assemble-uki.sh candidate_ukify_args has no --sign-initrd-pcrs
